# Temple Scroll Column 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 19 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**19:1** Take the first ram, and have Aaron and his sons place their hands on the ram's head.

**19:2** Slaughter the ram, collect its blood, and splash it against all sides of the altar.

**19:3** Cut the ram into sections, and wash the internal organs and the legs,

**19:4** then arrange them with the other pieces and the head.

**19:5** Burn the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering to the LORD — a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the LORD.

**19:6** Then take the second ram — this is the ram for the ordination —

**19:7** and have Aaron and his sons place their hands on the ram's head.

**19:8** Slaughter the ram, and take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe of Aaron,

**19:9** on the right earlobe of each of his sons, on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot.

**19:10** Splash the rest of the blood against all sides of the altar.

**19:11** Take some of the blood from the altar along with some anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments,

**19:12** and on his sons and their garments; this will consecrate him and his garments, along with his sons and their garments.

**19:13** From this ram take the fat, the broad fat tail, the fat covering the internal organs,

**19:14** the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh — since this is the ordination ram —

**19:15** plus one round loaf of bread, one oil cake, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that stands before Me.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 19 describes two distinct sacrificial acts during the priestly ordination. The first ram is entirely burned as a whole burnt offering. The second ram — the "ram of ordination" — involves a remarkable blood ceremony: blood is applied to the right ear, right thumb, and right big toe of each priest, symbolically dedicating their hearing, hands, and feet to God's service. The mixing of altar blood with anointing oil creates a uniquely powerful consecrating substance.*
